variants.headline: Assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out. It is a decisive parliamentary event, though it does not by itself describe what follows. An assessment of {target} should start with the withdrawal of confidence and avoid announcing a successor that this report does not identify.

Workers cannot live on parliamentary drama, but they cannot afford to ignore who exercises public power. The removal of a government matters because authority carries obligations to ordinary people. Labour should judge the politics by those obligations rather than by the entertainment value of a defeat.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A parliamentary defeat is decisive for office, but it need not be treated as a final moral verdict on every person or position involved. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.

variants.headline: Confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
variants.body:
